exact_statement: For a finite graph with an induced matching of M edges, q>=2 integer and beta>0, uniform independent spins u satisfy D(u||gamma_beta^free)>=M*(log((exp(beta)+q-1)/q)-beta/q). On n^d lattice boxes the liminf deficit per vertex is at least c_q(beta)/(3*2^(d-1))>0. For any fixed full-support product law pi, an alternative lower bound per vertex is 2*(min pi)^4*tanh(beta/2)^2/(3*2^(d-1)).
assumptions: finite simple graph with unit ferromagnetic Potts bonds
selected pairs form an induced matching
full support required for the nonuniform extension

exact_statement: For any finite simple graph G=(V,E), integer q>=2 and beta>=0, the uniform product spin law u and free zero-field Potts Gibbs law gamma_beta satisfy D(u||gamma_beta)>=|E|*(log((exp(beta)+q-1)/q)-beta/q), with equality for forests. For beta>0 and any cycle the inequality is strict. On Z^d the limiting deficit per vertex is at least d*c_q(beta)>0. At beta_MF=(q-1)*log(q-1)/(d*(q-2)), q>=3, the uniform and ordered mean-field product laws have equal scores and identical positive limiting entropy deficits, so neither satisfies L2.
assumptions: finite simple graph, unit ferromagnetic bonds, zero field
q>=3 and d>=1 for beta_MF comparison
growing lattice boxes for limiting statements
